draft_memo.title: Rooftop Solar Trends in Northstar
draft_memo.body:
In 2025, the Northstar region installed 120 megawatts of rooftop solar, which is an increase from 100 megawatts in 2024 [P01]. This represents a total increase of 20 megawatts in rooftop solar installations year-over-year [P01]. Northstar's residential rooftop solar installations increased from 40 to 55 megawatts between 2024 and 2025, marking a rise of 15 megawatts in this segment [P02]. Meanwhile, commercial installations saw a smaller increase, moving from 60 to 65 megawatts over the same period, which is an increase of 5 megawatts [P02]. The total increase in residential rooftop solar capacity from 2024 to 2025 is 15 megawatts, while commercial capacity increased by 5 megawatts [P02]. The overall trend shows a growing interest in rooftop solar installations in Northstar, with both residential and commercial sectors contributing to this growth [P01][P02].

Interpretation: The data shows that rooftop solar installations in Northstar increased in both residential and commercial sectors.

Limitations: The source does not provide information on the total number of installations or the specific types of solar technologies used. There is no detail on the geographic distribution of installations within Northstar. The data does not indicate the reasons behind the increases in capacity. Additionally, there is no information on the impact of these installations on energy consumption or savings. The source does not discuss any regulatory or policy changes that may have influenced these trends. There is no mention of the competitive landscape or market dynamics affecting rooftop solar installations. The memo lacks information on consumer adoption rates for rooftop solar installations in Northstar.
footnotes: [P02] Northstar residential and commercial solar data, 2025.
